<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6071badcbc26530b">Why is permission to send to a service insufficient to prevent data exposure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruntime-tickets">RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An attack can reuse the task&#x27;s permitted recipient to send secrets or extra content. A ticket must also require a trusted object validator and cumulative-amount limit. Recipient or tool-name checks alone do not express the delivery contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: the same endpoint can receive either an approved report or a secret key. The report validator rejects the key even when the endpoint is on the host allow-list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:runtime-tickets" data-paper-title="RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2315572f6cd842f">Should a request with a wrong recipient and an unknown object-validation result Defer or Deny?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruntime-tickets">RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deny takes precedence. Missing authority, any explicit failed obligation or exceeded budget denies. Only without failures can an unknown condition defer; all checks must pass to allow. Record the decision before the callback effect, and only Allow consumes quota and forwards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a wrong recipient remains Deny even when its validator is temporarily unavailable. An unknown check cannot turn known unauthorized access into waiting. A valid request reaches the callback only after its Allow record exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2315572f6cd842f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:runtime-tickets" data-paper-title="RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffcba3dc36c2439b">How does a ticket differ from a permission list declared by the Skill itself?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruntime-tickets">RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It attenuates a trusted host grant and cannot introduce unauthorized operations, resources or recipients. Obligations bind to the exact Skill version and source lines. Skill text is evidence to examine, not authority to approve access. The local compiler checks structural boundaries, not LLM semantic relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a Skill asking for an extra upload to other does not authorize other. Citing a nonexistent line 20 also fails source validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffcba3dc36c2439b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:runtime-tickets" data-paper-title="RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c934da4a778f2976">Do a valid HMAC chain and at-most-once callback establish a complete Supported proof and network exactly-once delivery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aruntime-tickets">RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neither. HMAC checks content and order in the supplied local records; a truncated prefix may remain valid. Full Supported needs a sealed, closed observation account. Callback failure leaves delivery unknown, so consumed quota is retained and the same ID is not resent. This is only local at-most-once invocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a server may receive data before the connection fails. Restoring quota and retrying could duplicate delivery. The component preserves that uncertainty rather than treating missing confirmation as no effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c934da4a778f2976">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rpl-95ce1341" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96cfb6b806b00ac8">Why does programmable retrieval return only explicitly printed documents to the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A program can retrieve, fuse, deduplicate, and rerank a large pool, but context receives only explicit outputs. This separates retrieval work from observation budget. Secretly appending intermediates bypasses program selection and invalidates the policy comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve 50 documents and print three after reranking. The model sees only those three, not the other 47.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96cfb6b806b00ac8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-387614f0d3ed6061">Why retain retrieval-program supervision for a wrong answer while masking its answer span?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A syntactically valid, executed program can contain useful retrieval structure even when the final answer is wrong. Mask wrong-answer supervision so it does not teach generation errors. Actors cannot see verifier gold, and environment observations are not policy-generated tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A program combines and deduplicates two retrieval routes correctly but the answerer copies a date incorrectly. Keep program supervision and mask the wrong date.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-387614f0d3ed6061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-82a8516fcb0b64ae">How does mutating retrieval structure while preserving the query differ from asking the model for a new query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keeping the query isolates retrieval mode, width, fusion, and reranking changes. A new query changes semantics along with control flow. Local mutations can restrict exploration, but using gold to produce correct documents is not a valid mutation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Widen retrieval from three to five under the same query to test evidence coverage. Adding answer keywords simultaneously confounds the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82a8516fcb0b64ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-908c2d6b9d2abe39">Does Meta&#x27;s release of full RPL code automatically make the local typed-program component a full reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Release improves provenance, not local fidelity. Local work still omits neural retrievers, cross-turn Python state, policy generation, GRPO, and distillation. The main project&#x27;s CC-BY-NC and vendored licenses still apply. Public code is not permission to copy or upgrade evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Having factory blueprints does not mean a small pipe simulator makes the same product. The real execution path and costs still need verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文信息, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-908c2d6b9d2abe39">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5e7b293a86bb7f2">How does the local restricted RPL program control retrieval, fusion, and final output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It allows at most four distinct queries, prescribed retrieval and reranking widths, real fusion of multi-route results, and a cap on printed documents. Conflicting contents for one ID are rejected, and reranking cannot add unretrieved documents. Local execution interprets data classes and an injected SDK, not arbitrary Python or the paper&#x27;s token limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieving twenty items and printing three legitimately separates compute and observation. Quietly injecting an unretrieved document during reranking breaks provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5e7b293a86bb7f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-world-of-swecraft-5a1942f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-10201c0f398592ac">Why does World of SWEcraft model a package ecosystem maintained by several agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing one isolated issue does not capture cross-project dependencies or long-term effects. Maintainers continuously change packages, affecting downstream users and requiring coordinated releases alongside local progress. Activity volume does not measure ecosystem quality; verify downstream functionality and resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A package changes a function signature and passes its own tests, but two dependent packages no longer import. Single-issue tests can miss that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10201c0f398592ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac28edabd2d0ac9a">Why validate collective improvement on hidden downstream packages instead of only agent-maintained microbenchmarks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The group may overfit visible benchmarks while breaking real dependents. Installing frozen releases in unseen downstream packages tests compatibility and benefits. Failures stay in strict or carry aggregation rather than being dropped, and instruction counts do not measure wall-clock speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A function specialized for self-test inputs can improve a microbenchmark while breaking a downstream parser. Hidden dependencies reveal the regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac28edabd2d0ac9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ebc669cc7428ed58">How does persistent multi-session collaboration differ from one indefinitely long group chat?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents hand off through repositories, issues, PRs, releases, and durable memory, with separate session permissions and budgets. Shared artifacts preserve work without replaying every discussion, but coordination, ownership, and versioning still cost. More agents or larger models do not automatically produce more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One maintainer releases a new version and a dependent library adapts using release artifacts, without all chat history being visible every turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ebc669cc7428ed58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3324ecfdacb047a6">How do strict and carry aggregate speed in correctness-failure rounds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strict assigns failed package tasks speed ratio one; carry uses the most recent passing ratio. Both retain all tasks and take a geometric mean. Instruction-count gains are not wall-clock speedup. Local formulas do not execute the ecosystem or reproduce its 55K sessions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If an optimization breaks tests, keep the package in the denominator. Carry uses its last valid speed, not a faster failing run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tracer-f2f8d03e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1efe2d57b68e50f">Why can a large tool catalog consume context without surfacing the right next action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keeping every description is costly, while static Top-K may omit the next interface. TRACER predicts a subset from executed transitions and current context so discovery adapts to progress. Candidate prediction does not replace argument validation or successful calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After identity lookup, account retrieval is more likely than rereading a thousand tools. If the user cancels, context should change the recommendation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1efe2d57b68e50f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a03d84108db990af">Why does a tool trie use the complete within-turn call prefix instead of just the previous tool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same previous tool can occur in distinct workflows. A full prefix preserves path identity and retrieves real training transitions. Context similarity adds current intent, with learned weight and temperature. Unknown prefixes fall back to catalog search rather than force an unseen path onto the nearest old branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Search→download may lead to parsing, whereas authenticate→download may need permission checking. Download alone conflates them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a03d84108db990af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee6c2772d37a26ac">Why learn the mix of frequency and context priors rather than simply add them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent tools can be wrong for current context, while semantic transitions may have few samples. Two linear heads use five state features to set mixing weight and temperature. Temperature changes the confidence gate, not order. Coverage and calibration still matter; frequency is not success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A prefix usually leads to A, but the current context resembles past transitions to B. Reduce the frequency weight rather than copy blindly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee6c2772d37a26ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6d187227006150a">Why must cross-fitting exclude the target trajectory&#x27;s entire fold rather than only hide the current label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Other steps from that trajectory can affect trie counts and edge-context means. Hiding the label alone still leaks its structure. Each signal must use an index excluding the full fold, and standardization is fitted on training folds. Training real heads on synthetic vectors is not real tool-selection capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The target tool may be absent from loss input yet already counted in the all-data index, revealing its own answer path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6d187227006150a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-structural-signal-retriever-c1b3c953" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-164006635fc0f00e">Why does SSR start with discovering which agent to consider in a large directory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sending every capability description to a model raises selection cost. SSR uses discrete public-description signals to build an inverted candidate pool for later decisions. Matching is interpretable and literal, so paraphrases with no shared signal can legitimately yield nothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An invoice signal in both a task and a capability card creates a candidate. Disjoint terminology may not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-164006635fc0f00e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2848f9d257695af3">Why does SSR return an empty pool on no lexical match rather than claim a semantically similar agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structural signals are terms and adjacent phrases from explicit fields. IDF gives no semantic score to unmatched content. Inverted lookup skips only zero-score candidates and retains the same lexical ranking. An empty pool exposes missing evidence; arbitrary fallback is not semantic understanding by SSR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A card says invoice, and a nonoverlapping paraphrase gets no hit. This is a lexical coverage gap, not a discovered synonym.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2848f9d257695af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-192b9bf0a837b4c8">Why do inverted SSR and an exhaustive scan of the same IDF score rank positive matches identically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All IDFs are positive, so the postings union collects exactly cards sharing at least one query signal and excludes zero scores. Rank by the same score, match count, and ID tie-breaker. Savings come from skipping disjoint cards, not changing semantics. No hit means an empty pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Of a thousand cards, only ten share a term. Scoring those ten returns the exhaustive scan&#x27;s positive ranking without fake fallbacks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-192b9bf0a837b4c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b24b4dfd98b871d6">What constraints govern repeated words, the 64-signal limit, and empty_pool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Signals are binary and deduplicated. Frequency only affects unigram truncation above the limit, followed by deterministic bigram filling. No hit returns empty_pool without calling a provider for an invented answer. API failures and illegal indexes stay failures. There is no real local LLM orchestration success metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeating search ten times does not yield tenfold score, and a zero lexical match cannot silently switch to full-directory semantic retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b24b4dfd98b871d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-leash-edca97db" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d41c3c5dadc1bc88">Why does LEASH run a weaker model and hand off only in riskier states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong calls throughout cost more; weak-only execution may fail in critical states. Risk-triggered takeover trades task outcomes against resource use. Handoffs are not free and risk scores are not inherently probabilities. Account for complete execution and results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use a small model for routine file search and a stronger one for rare recovery states. Value depends on takeover count and actual delivery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d41c3c5dadc1bc88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc752aad38fc797e">Why keep using unexecuted Shadow actions after the stronger model takes over?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Handoff mitigates weak-model failure but does not prevent the strong model drifting. Weak shadow representations offer a cheap reference for periodic review without executing shadow actions. Distance to the failure reference is not calibrated failure probability or a fixed test takeover quota.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The strong model is about to delete while the weak shadow suggests checking permissions. Trigger review without running both actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc752aad38fc797e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0d0812a090585e4">Why isn&#x27;t a reference-distance score a calibrated failure probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares the weak representation&#x27;s Mahalanobis distances to Pass and Fail means. Higher values only indicate relative proximity to failure. Shift, covariance, and representation geometry affect thresholds, and target routing proportions are not test quotas. Calibrate on references rather than map scores directly to percentages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Score two does not imply 20% failure; a different scale or task distribution can change risk at the same score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0d0812a090585e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18c5ccd7b7190180">Why calibrate the runtime gate on each task&#x27;s maximum score, and when does Shadow trigger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibrate reference risk on maximum action score per task, keeping all observations from a task in the same out-of-fold split. Step quantiles change the overall escalation rate. After handoff, probe every three steps from the first strong action: 1, 4, 7, with at most six interventions and a stop after two changes to strong actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Starting checks only in the third interval misses first-step risk. Splitting steps from one task across train and validation leaks task features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18c5ccd7b7190180">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-agent-harness-91c2ebf3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c94f465af04e5cf">Why not use equally expensive reasoning for every small decision in Jev Agent Harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool workflows have bounded decisions, some suitable for a cheap decider and others needing more reasoning. Explicit delegation with fallback lets savings and error costs define the scope. A cheap decider is not automatically good for open tasks; validate it on states it actually encounters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model may decide whether to keep a candidate record. An open explanation with missing evidence may still require the main model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c94f465af04e5cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9b8fa18e0639f8f">Why calibrate delegation thresholds by decision type on the agent&#x27;s own shadow trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Closed-loop execution reaches states after errors, which clean offline multiple choice does not cover. Tool and argument choices also have different risks and benefits. Compare decision and strong models on matched examples, choose reliable thresholds by task value and cost, and fall back on uncertain or unseen classes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A small model chooses tools correctly but often supplies wrong arguments. Give the categories separate gates instead of applying one overall accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9b8fa18e0639f8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5e0239b2d9b5b36">How does a cost- and task-value threshold differ from a fixed 0.7 confidence gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Utility uses paired correctness differences between the decision and strong models plus saved call cost. Select a confidence suffix whose bins are all nonnegative. A constant ignores class, error cost, and overconfidence. Fitting is not infallible; the paper retains failed calibration and no-gain additional training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A high-stakes error can outweigh a small saving, while a recoverable decision may tolerate a lower delegation threshold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5e0239b2d9b5b36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-92de0166e9d9fec7">Should unknown classes or undersampled categories use the nearest threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Default bins require at least twenty rows, keep equal confidence together, and merge undersized tails. Too few rows for a category, no eligible suffix, or an unknown type means fall back to the strong model. Fit uses calibration validation only; runtime sees no gold or strong-model answers. Local handwritten callbacks test the contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three argument decisions cannot calibrate a reliable threshold. Fall back rather than borrowing a different tool class&#x27;s threshold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92de0166e9d9fec7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">

<span id="paper-agent-research-gemini-minecraft-c1e2611e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e601316159b12b01">Why study teamwork through long-horizon Minecraft completion rather than single-instruction following?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exploration, resource gathering, crafting, and combat create dependencies in time and materials, with new state along the way. Multiple agents, observation, and shared information support progress. One full completion demonstrates a possibility but not a probability or causal gain from one module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Mining and food gathering can be divided across roles. A note that mining is done does not produce crafting material if it was never acquired.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bec7e1165a81dee5">Why can&#x27;t the Observer and shared notes replace each executing agent&#x27;s actual environment feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries help coordinate but can lag or miss local changes. Programs must use world responses to determine success. Programmatic action, durable notes, and multi-session collaboration support long tasks together. A chat claim cannot advance dependent steps, and a described case is not a local run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A note says a bridge was fixed, but another agent sees it destroyed. Update from current observation instead of trusting the old note.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bec7e1165a81dee5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a451cee9a3ff262f">How compare evidence and costs for four collaborating agents versus one long-running agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parallel roles can divide exploration and execution but add communication, duplication, and coordination. The paper gives one long success in a random Easy world, not multiseed controls establishing reliability or cost advantage. Completion does not mean four agents generally beat one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Four agents can gather resources faster or all collect the same item. One success cannot isolate teamwork from extra compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a451cee9a3ff262f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5f10c30d9efc8b8">Can a 27-hour completion be stated as 100% success or a local executable capability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One case has no independent repetition denominator. Roughly 24,000 calls are the authors&#x27; costs. Local work records literature and cost without commercial calls, game execution, GPU receipts, or an Evolve operator. Formal interaction notation is not a Minecraft implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One game completion is one successful case, not ten successes or a local receipt based on the authors&#x27; video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5f10c30d9efc8b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">

<span id="paper-agent-research-diviner-0cc63af7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca9a7eaa53802c0f">Why log evidence availability time as well as event time during incident diagnosis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An investigator may not have later aggregates or conclusions when an event happens. Diviner requires matching incident, target, and window with available time no later than as-of. That separates contemporaneous material from final explanations, but structural compliance does not prove entailment or root cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An error at 10:00 appears in a report generated at 11:00. A 10:30 investigation cannot use that report despite its earlier event time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca9a7eaa53802c0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9cacdbf91e3b740">Why does a tool timeout neither support nor refute a root-cause hypothesis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A timeout means no valid observation, not that the service is healthy or faulty. Evidence must match incident, target, time window, and availability. Similar incidents are clues only. Adapting investigation is distinct from publishing a workflow or executing mitigation, which requires separate authority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A ranking-log query times out. Mark unknown and gather evidence differently rather than conclude ranking was healthy or use a later postmortem as contemporaneous evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9cacdbf91e3b740">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ac48fe99644b2db">Why govern live investigation adaptation differently from publishing persistent knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A current plan can adapt to new evidence with local scope. Shared workflows influence future incidents and require a new version, replay validation, and artifact-owner approval. The paper does not authorize autonomous production mitigation or turn observational MTTR changes into randomized causal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Add a config lookup to this incident. Rewriting the team-wide playbook needs independent validation and an owner release.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ac48fe99644b2db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e7a7715b53924c">What identity and time constraints must evidence satisfy before entering EvidenceLedger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind records to the current incident, target, and investigation window. Distinguish event time from evidence availability, which must not exceed as-of. Otherwise unrelated logs or later summaries can be mistaken for evidence available then. Local tests verify provenance and governance, not root cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A predawn error summarized in the morning is not known to the predawn investigator. A similar error from another incident cannot be mixed in.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e7a7715b53924c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-aria-04eaa6e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-61400377d7f00fa0">Why repair an early partial trajectory rather than just summarize failure at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early mistakes propagate across agent messages. Cutting and continuing during a run can prevent amplification. ARIA learns when and where to intervene and how to continue, but must execute the patch to verify it. Replacing a suffix does not prove diagnosis or exact environment rollback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A message uses the wrong unit and later agents copy it. Repair before propagation rather than only explain it after completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-61400377d7f00fa0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-72d8e93a8b1ee2a9">Why may a repaired trajectory propose a pending tool call but not write a successful tool result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Results must come from execution; otherwise the patch fabricates evidence. The cut preserves the observed prefix, and continuation proposes new actions before comparison with a fresh control. Structural validity does not prove correct attribution or repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Proposing to rerun tests is legal. Saying all tests passed in the continuation is not; execute and observe them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72d8e93a8b1ee2a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d5c547a0a9d2f33">Why require a patched pass and fresh-control failure together for verified repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A patched success alone can result from retry randomness or environmental changes. If the fresh control also succeeds, improvement cannot be attributed to a necessary patch. The pair rules out simple retries as repair evidence but is not exact causal replay of a full framework. The paper reconstructs continuation context within a stated scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tests pass after patching, but also pass on a fresh unpatched rerun. Do not use that pair as verified repair training data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d5c547a0a9d2f33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7108f55dcf61f947">What hard constraints apply to the cut event, patch types, and size?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cut retains the referenced observed event and, if nonempty, must precede the identified bad event. A patch allows at most eight events and 12,000 canonical JSON characters, requires nonconflicting IDs, and cannot replay the old suffix with new IDs. Only assistant messages and pending calls are allowed, not fabricated tool results. No five-stage model training ran locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Propose another order lookup, but do not insert an invented tool observation that it was paid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
