<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7108f55dcf61f947">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rated-710146a7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d43794df2d72755">Why rerank by execution reliability when a tool is semantically relevant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The best matching description may refer to a tool that fails, times out, or is unavailable. RATED retrieves semantic Top-K first, then combines static metadata and per-tool online feedback. Reliability complements relevance without justifying a tool that cannot solve the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Favor the weather API that still works over a frequently timing-out equivalent, not an irrelevant reliable calculator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d43794df2d72755">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3a60a5875bf4cde">Why does execution feedback update only the LinUCB arm for the tool actually selected?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only execution exposes success, error, or timeout. Unchosen outcomes are counterfactual. Per-tool updates avoid blaming all candidates for one failure, while discounting reduces old reliability evidence over time. Semantic top-K supplies candidates; exploration does not prove an uncalled tool is better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If tool A times out, update A. Do not mark unused B successful; retain uncertainty until it is tried.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3a60a5875bf4cde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-34d38c6c74c040d3">What do the frozen dual encoder and online discounted LinUCB adapt to?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The offline encoder supplies semantic query-tool representations and stays frozen in deployment. LinUCB updates each arm from actual feedback and discounts older evidence as reliability changes. Bandit reranking is not online retraining of the text encoder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Successful calls after service recovery can raise arm value while encoder parameters remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34d38c6c74c040d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e3acf45069aec6">How does γ affect history for the selected tool in discounted LinUCB?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decay the selected arm&#x27;s diagonal A and b by γ, then add current squared features and execution feedback. Older evidence loses influence, and A also controls exploration uncertainty, so this is not just changing a success rate. The local encoder trained briefly, but the authorized tool binding failed; bandit updates are not tool success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Recent timeouts can outweigh a long success history under decay. Permanent cumulative statistics may hide the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e3acf45069aec6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-workflow-32efeb08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e21801a615beb116">Why evaluate cheap decisions per completed delivery instead of per invocation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents combine decisions, tools, and retries. Local savings can increase downstream failures and reruns. Jev Workflow counts all resources required for delivery so cheaper decisions and extra attempts share one denominator. Report different success subsets separately rather than advertise local latency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving half a second per decision may cost three extra attempts. The user pays for all of them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e21801a615beb116">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f67a6f111ad8004f">Why might faster individual decisions raise total resources per successful delivery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Errors can cause retries, failed recovery, or premature completion. Resource per success includes cost and time for every attempt divided by successes. Matched successes compare smooth paths only and cannot replace all-attempt delivery or hide failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A route half as expensive per attempt may succeed twice in ten tries, making it costlier per delivery than a slower route that succeeds eight times.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f67a6f111ad8004f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-be33fb879417f3dd">What do matched-success and all-attempt delivery each measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matched-success compares resources only on task/run pairs where both configurations succeed, isolating cost along successful paths. All-attempt includes failed resources and all successes to measure delivery. Conditioning on joint success can hide one configuration&#x27;s many failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three jointly solved tasks can show faster decisions without revealing failures among the seven others. Interpret both views.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be33fb879417f3dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c39238132ac53294">Why not compute a tidy ratio with zero successes, missing pairs, or invalid resource values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cost per success is undefined at zero successes. Missing task/run pairs invalidate comparisons, and negative or nonfinite resources are invalid observations. Report or reject these states rather than delete failures to repair a denominator. The infrastructure consumes real paired traces and neither loads nor fabricates Jev weights or API outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Do not add ε to an all-failure denominator or copy a paper row as a local run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c39238132ac53294">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mingbird-bbd1f960" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce08018ff6229f8e">Why does MingBird focus on small models doing long multi-tool tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small models have limited context, tool understanding, and error recovery. Loading all tools and all history adds pressure. MingBird organizes tools, execution loops, and completion checks under resource constraints. Components do not establish reliable arbitrary long-horizon capability; verify actual deliverables.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file-and-database task first shows the relevant domain, then executes steps and verifies output rather than reading the whole catalog and declaring completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce08018ff6229f8e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d9bfd00f5a7bc2d8">Why reintroduce the original task and plan and check artifacts after the model says it is done?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A long trajectory can forget requirements or confuse executed actions with delivery. Checking the original exposes missing files, missing verification, and early stopping. Loop detection and bounded format rescue address runtime faults, not model knowledge. Budget actual UTF-8 bytes rather than character counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Creating a file does not satisfy a task that also requires a test report. Re-read the original artifact list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d9bfd00f5a7bc2d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fd8604251771df1">What do domain routing and flattened schemas trade off against showing all original tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing narrows the tool domain. Presenting required arguments when schemas are large reduces formatting burden and irrelevant interfaces. Optional arguments can still matter, and user constraints cannot be dropped. This changes harness input and recovery, not base architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A tool has ten parameters and two required ones. Start with a simplified schema but still honor a user-requested optional filter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fd8604251771df1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-797790e34afbed84">How are duplicate-call signatures and prefill budget computed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use tool name and canonical JSON arguments, so key order does not distinguish calls. Block the sixth repeat before execution and correct after fifteen consecutive no-output actions. Prefill counts UTF-8 bytes. JSON rescue parses registered tools only without eval; this is not a full GUI product or sandbox.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reversed key order cannot evade duplicate detection. A CJK character can use multiple UTF-8 bytes, so character counts understate input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-797790e34afbed84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cera-moa-0d23f31e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2b4d20645f640f0">Why does CERA-MoA assign samples to experts familiar with them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calling the same number and set of models on all questions can waste resources and hinder specialization. Familiarity guides selection and training allocation. It is a routing signal, not proof of a correct answer; verify outcomes and total compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Code and math experts may join different samples. Role names alone do not establish effective division of labor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2b4d20645f640f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a271c323eae1f5d">Why use familiarity-based expert selection and assign training samples back to experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing choices and training assignments feed back: assignments shape future expertise. Middle-layer representations estimate familiarity, a cumulative threshold chooses how many experts to use, and targeted training reinforces specialization. Changing only routing while training everyone identically may not sustain distinct expertise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Send code cases toward a code-familiar expert and language cases elsewhere. Ambiguous samples may activate more experts rather than use one fixed team.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a271c323eae1f5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4b34cd474558571">How does a cumulative threshold differ from fixed Top-2 expert selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-2 uses the same number per task. Cumulative selection adapts to score concentration: easy cases can use fewer experts and uncertain cases more. Variable counts change cost, so compare quality with total compute rather than infer efficiency from average routed count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use one clearly dominant expert or several with similar scores instead of always calling two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4b34cd474558571">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64e00323a4a519f4">What does directed training assignment update beyond inference-only routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CERA-MoA also sends training samples to designated experts, letting routing and capability co-evolve. Selection masks alone train nothing. Local tests cover familiarity routing and a directed-update reference, not paper-scale expert training. Three-seed state statistics do not establish capability evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A sample assignment to expert A does not show A received a gradient update. Verify parameter changes and independent task results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64e00323a4a519f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-repoatlas-e75f59d2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c0ccc4c019a0e9e">What map does RepoAtlas build first for an unfamiliar large repository?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reading files one at a time can lose global structure, while a broad overview cannot locate symbols. RepoAtlas combines topology and precise source entry points so agents can understand dependencies and inspect code. Navigation does not replace source evidence, and stale structure can misdirect later edits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For login bugs, trace authentication and API dependencies before opening the validation function. Module names do not reveal the real conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c0ccc4c019a0e9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5335c0c305107d48">Why refresh visual topology and the precise text index together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Topology shows module dependencies, and text locates actual editable symbols. If views disagree, a correct graph can point to an obsolete file. Select–project–refresh chooses task-related subgraphs under budget and keeps both views grounded in common sources. A diagram does not replace source evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After moving a function, update its graph edges and indexed location; refreshing only one can leave nonexistent paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5335c0c305107d48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-054bffbc80cbfc11">What is the trade-off between a task-related code subgraph and a whole-repository summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A subgraph keeps relevant relations within budget but can miss remote dependencies. A whole summary covers more at lower detail. Refresh selection as implementation and feedback change. A one-time snapshot or visible graph is not improved code understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Editing authentication needs callers and configuration. If initially omitted, failed tests can justify expanding the subgraph.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-054bffbc80cbfc11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e19879cd431db5b">Does the local bounded text view implement a real multimodal SWE-bench repository environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public observations produce a budgeted text view and selection/refresh state. It does not claim real browser or SWE-bench integration. Indexes, edges, and budgets are checkable; visual topology generation, model consumption, and repair outcomes need separate execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten nodes and source locations show view data exists, not that a model viewed a graph and fixed an issue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e19879cd431db5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hcrg" data-paper-title="Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hcrg-d21831b9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f0b7b0eab559fdf">Why identify parent dependencies before migrating callers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahcrg">Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parent classes, imports, and called interfaces shape assumptions in dependent code. Migrating resolvable parents first stabilizes context. HCRG extracts AST structure up to three hops. Static graphs cannot cover all dynamic calls, and unresolved symbols should not be matched to arbitrary same-name definitions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Migrating a superclass constructor signature first makes it easier to update subclasses consistently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12464">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.12464-hcrg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f0b7b0eab559fdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hcrg" data-paper-title="Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-62471e72ac894fa6">Why can&#x27;t a cyclic dependency graph have a node-wise parents-first topological order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahcrg">Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nodes in a directed cycle depend on one another, so no linear order satisfies all edges. Identify strongly connected components and separate ordering across components from migration within them. AST context reveals this limit, but it does not invent a cycle-breaking method the paper never defines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A calls B and B imports A. Analyze them as a cycle, not as though migrating A first satisfies all parent dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12464">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.12464-hcrg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62471e72ac894fa6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hcrg" data-paper-title="Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-61a331bb82962207">How does three-hop structural context differ from vector retrieval over 800-character chunks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahcrg">Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Vector chunks return textually similar fragments. Structural retrieval follows inheritance, calls, and imports, potentially finding related code with different words. Both miss things. Some paper metrics on a single repository decline, so structure does not uniformly improve migrations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A utility&#x27;s name has little lexical overlap with a migration issue, but a call edge still brings it into context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12464">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.12464-hcrg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-61a331bb82962207">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hcrg" data-paper-title="Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-febd84dd63974652">How should static graphs handle local-variable shadowing and unresolved symbols?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahcrg">Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same names can denote different definitions, and local binding hides globals. Do not connect unresolved calls to arbitrary same-name repository nodes. Retain scope and unresolved status, then retrieve only known structure. Local support is bounded Python AST, not all dynamic calls or other paper languages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a function assigns a local object to a global tool&#x27;s name, later calls use the local binding, not a global node with the same text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12464">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.12464-hcrg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-febd84dd63974652">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-feedback-scaffold-b914bba8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-86b6f2fda9fa582b">Why are fully unguided exploration and always giving answers both difficult for weaker long-horizon agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unguided exploration may yield too few successful experiences. Always providing correct actions can teach reliance on help. Feedback Scaffold changes support during training so early learning starts and later decisions are independent. Evaluate capability after removing the scaffold rather than count guided success as autonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Demonstrate the next step at first, later give observations only. Continuing to choose actions during tests hides independent ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86b6f2fda9fa582b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32e4e27887fc3581">Why start with action guidance and shift to observation enrichment later?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct hints lower early exploration difficulty and yield learnable traces, but continued demonstration can make policy dependent. Later enriched observations retain evidence support while returning decisions to the agent, gradually reducing scaffolding. The phases serve different purposes and should not share constant strong hints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tell a beginner to find a key first. Later describe the lock and let the agent choose, rather than reveal the whole sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32e4e27887fc3581">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c298fb923271d9a8">Why evaluate scaffolded completion separately from autonomous completion after removing support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scaffolding can simplify decisions or add evidence, so success reflects both policy and support. Removal tests whether training left transferable decisions. Report visible help and do not pool different information conditions. A phase-scheduling diagnostic does not replace real transfer after training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If testing still tells the model to read config first, it measures following the hint. Autonomous evaluation requires discovering that action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c298fb923271d9a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e00f463b6f22a769">Can the local first-step workflow be read from hidden AgentTask.plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use only a workflow explicitly supplied in public observation, then state summaries. Hidden plans never reach policy. No LLM training or real rollouts ran. The controlled path verifies isolation and schedules, not long-task learning from oracle-induced perfect scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A three-step reference plan in a fixture must not be disguised as an environment hint; that leaks the answer rather than enriches observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e00f463b6f22a769">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-prime" data-paper-title="SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-swe-prime-e014601a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cabb17e601059f07">Why might a successful trajectory still be a poor full SFT target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-prime">SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success can include redundant exploration, risky commands, or steps the current model cannot learn. SWE-Prime filters trajectories by process, outcome, and representativeness, then selects segments by contribution, learnability, and risk. Outcome success does not endorse every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A bug fix ultimately passes after accidentally deleting and restoring a file. Do not teach deletion as a good action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27449">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27449-swe-prime/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cabb17e601059f07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-prime" data-paper-title="SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-09148f0475ab00b9">Why retain complete context but apply SFT loss only to selected semantic segments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-prime">SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unselected spans may be necessary causal context for later behavior even if redundant, dangerous, or unhelpful to imitate. Masking separates readable context from training targets. The model sees the real process while learning useful, learnable actions; not every token in a successful trajectory deserves supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep a failed dangerous command to explain a repair, without rewarding the model for generating that command.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27449">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27449-swe-prime/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09148f0475ab00b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-prime" data-paper-title="SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe246fc75fa9c390">What different data-quality problems do whole-trajectory and within-trajectory segment selection solve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-prime">SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectory selection chooses useful complete experiences by outcome, process, and representativeness. Segment selection chooses contributing, learnable, lower-risk behavior within them. Good traces can contain redundancy, and good fragments can come from failed overall runs. Sample selection and supervision are distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep a passing repair&#x27;s complete execution as context, but exclude irrelevant dependency installation from imitation targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27449">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27449-swe-prime/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe246fc75fa9c390">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-prime" data-paper-title="SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7dac67bcfc67dd77">Do local filtering results show a code LLM was trained or SWE-bench ran?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-prime">SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local filtering strategies share an observation and tool interface without training a code model or running official SWE-bench. Verify that loss masks cover only selected spans, context stays complete, and data splits remain isolated. Small tool-routing metrics are not code-repair gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: More stable local routes after removing risky segments do not reproduce the paper&#x27;s outcome with one tenth of its code traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27449">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27449-swe-prime/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7dac67bcfc67dd77">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-traceml-cea4f922" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9262e749f8e77b96">Why does TraceML record the whole human ML development process rather than just the highest-scoring model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final code and scores hide exploration, abandonment, revisiting, and budget allocation. TraceML records decisions and versions as planning evidence. Observed human behavior is not proof of optimality; downstream use requires independent tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A small final model conceals the failed larger-model experiment that identified the bottleneck and motivated the pivot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9262e749f8e77b96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d61cb02f607c749">Why do versions, action intent, and edit size teach planning patterns better than score curves alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scores show outcomes but cannot distinguish architecture exploration, tuning, or returning to an old approach. Linking edits to intent and effect reveals stage changes and reopened approaches for a prior. Patterns in human traces still need agent validation and are not optimal by default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two score drops can come from trying a feature or accidentally deleting configuration. Version and action records tell whether to continue or revert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d61cb02f607c749">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-07360ef008b25b07">How do human stage alternation and revisiting old ideas differ from a monotonic plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Humans move among analysis, implementation, and evaluation and revisit hypotheses after new evidence. A monotonic plan can discard abandoned paths permanently. A prior can encourage useful revisits, not enforce cycles on every task. Closer behavior does not guarantee better scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: New validation identifies a data problem, making a previously abandoned simple model worth reconsidering instead of increasing complexity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07360ef008b25b07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e992817dbacafea4">Can TraceML&#x27;s failure-reflection prior keep reading hidden routes on validation or test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Learn the prior on train, then freeze it and act on actual tool feedback without hidden answers or routes. PlanBench stage and reopen counts are mechanism diagnostics, and ToolRoute is not the full Kaggle experiment. They are different evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Adjust after a public test error, but do not reopen a solution by reading the reference plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e992817dbacafea4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-topas-ae42000c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-75c29be356dd9dec">Why does TOPAS consider the workflow&#x27;s longest remaining path rather than only individual progress?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One request can block downstream work, so local priority can increase tail waiting. Critical-path estimates include dependencies and remaining work, then trade them against prefix reuse, transfer, and preemption. Optimize completion time, not cache hits alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A short request unblocks five later nodes and may deserve priority over a long request that has already run extensively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75c29be356dd9dec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-844b8a90e779e693">Why not optimize shared-cache scheduling for prefix hit rate alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hits improve local reuse but can delay critical workflow paths and incur expensive transfers or preemption. TOPAS combines longest remaining path, downstream reuse, and movement cost, with aging against starvation. Hit rate is an intermediate measure, not whole-task completion time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Serving many high-hit small requests can block a nearly finished main workflow. Sacrificing hits to unblock the critical path can deliver sooner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-844b8a90e779e693">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3ba7f4b88395eaa">What latency risks do critical-path priority and aging address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Critical-path priority identifies requests delaying whole workflows. Aging raises priority with wait time so tasks are not repeatedly starved. These address dependencies and fairness, alongside cache reuse and movement. No single priority makes every task fastest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Aging eventually helps a short chain skipped for low cache reuse, while a long chain&#x27;s blocked node still matters for critical-path latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3ba7f4b88395eaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-53eb77d8871172b0">Do simulated prefix hits and ToolRoute results prove real LLM serving speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite simulates prefix reuse, critical path, and aging. Stateful tools do not exercise real KV serving kernels. Paper mean/p99 JCT comes from real system experiments requiring requests, memory, movement, and wall-clock timing. Proxy costs and hit counts are not convertible directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three extra hits do not save three identical prefill intervals. Prefix lengths and scheduling overhead matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53eb77d8871172b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-progrouter-c8bea01c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b2e86e619f312c8">Why does ProgRouter track changing model needs during one task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
