<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reasoning requirements vary by stage. Always using a strong model is costly; a weak model can stall. ProgRouter routes each next call by current progress. Static rankings do not quantify help now, and real gains depend on time and call budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model locates a file, then a stronger model handles complex inference. Overall rank alone does not justify using it for both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b2e86e619f312c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a4bcdd40231ca7a">Why predict marginal progress for routing instead of comparing average model accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A stronger model may offer little progress in one state but unblock another. Marginal progress uses completion, trend, and quality to value the next call against time and long-run budget. Average accuracy misses stage differences, and predictions still require execution feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model can repair formatting while a difficult proof needs stronger reasoning. Calling the average best on every step wastes budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a4bcdd40231ca7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-22fc3889a20630c0">How does a quality, time, and long-run-cost meta-gate compare with always choosing the cheapest model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cheap calls can accumulate retries and cost more overall. A meta-gate trades predicted progress, call price, and budget pressure, sometimes paying more for a better candidate. Report delivery quality, time, and total budget instead of just per-call cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three cheap calls stall while one expensive call solves it. If the expensive call also stalls, execution must override the prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22fc3889a20630c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1d2177e87e77e3d">Does the local frozen program router have the same scope as the paper&#x27;s multi-model progress predictor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work compiles verified tool choices into routes, freezes them for validation and test, and executes. Mini-suite checks cover progress, meta-gating, and downgrade, not paper models, serving resources, or full benchmarks. Proxy costs and program selection are not measured joules or citation precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reading two fewer candidates does not imply the same energy saving on HumanEval without actual model and hardware measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1d2177e87e77e3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-adavdr-576e1cf8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac1cf4aa14f91dfb">Why judge tool necessity relative to the target model&#x27;s capabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Do not repeat external calls for things the model already handles; use tools for missing information. Necessity depends on model and evidence, not an unconditional prohibition. Reflect when intermediate evidence is unreliable rather than minimize calls at the cost of needed checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Clear colors can be read directly, but small text may need zoom or retrieval. A weaker vision model changes that boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac1cf4aa14f91dfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-88d371dfdcbc173d">Why separate tool necessity from fallback reflection on unreliable evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Necessity decides whether to gather external evidence; reflection decides whether existing evidence needs another check. Capability-based filtering saves unnecessary calls and redundancy penalties guide training. Ignoring unreliable evidence merely to call less can hurt video research, so minimum call count is not optimal by itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Do not search to confirm visible running. If identity clues disagree, recheck rather than keep the first conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88d371dfdcbc173d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e89b590dd2f51e78">How does a redundancy-aware reward differ from penalizing every call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Redundancy penalties target unnecessary or repeated calls while preserving useful evidence gathering. A flat penalty can deter necessary tools. Evaluate answer reward and reflection as well, since recovery and verification may require justified extra cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeating a search with no new information can be redundant, while checking conflicting sources may be essential.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e89b590dd2f51e78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bebf5ef6d4303580">How should local ToolRoute success be reported alongside cost and video scope?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retain added verifier cost and state that local runs use an oracle-free stateful tool environment, not the paper&#x27;s video data or full VDR system. Perfect PlanBench is a mechanism diagnostic. Fallback counts or success under another protocol are not video research gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Report that an extra verification step bought local success rather than claim higher success and fewer video calls from the same result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bebf5ef6d4303580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-smith-3e4d7833" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaa53cee12cd56e6">Why does SMITH learn to create reusable tools rather than only use existing ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed tools may not cover new tasks, and rewriting one-off code wastes effort. Building and later using tools links interface and implementation to real use. Code generation does not establish usefulness; format, execution, and downstream answers can fail independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeated cleaning needs can justify a dedicated tool. Keep it only if later tasks can call it correctly and finish cleaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaa53cee12cd56e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-26ea08414f79720d">Why jointly train tool creation and use in one policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewarding runnable code alone can produce awkward tools or tools that fail new tasks. Training only use cannot improve design. Mixed build and held-out use connect schema, execution, and outcome signals to encourage reusable abstractions. Passing examples is not independent problem solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A tool hard-codes a training constant and earns execution reward, but held-out calls expose the lack of reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26ea08414f79720d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b59b77f1e41a46c9">Why aren&#x27;t schema, code execution, and final answer rewards interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A schema only needs to parse. Code execution only needs to run without crashing. The final result tests whether the task was solved. Separate signals expose different faults. Harder problems should encourage abstraction, not more hard-coded examples passed off as generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A function has a valid signature and returns a number using the wrong formula. It passes the first two checks but fails the answer check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b59b77f1e41a46c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83a7dab631c78030">Is the local structured-plan tool equivalent to a Python execution sandbox?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work separates build and use and runs three verifiers, but uses controlled plans without Qwen3-4B, a Python sandbox, or Reasoning-Gym. Generation and reuse counts verify control flow, not paper code-tool training effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule interpreter can execute an add node without safely compiling or running arbitrary model-generated Python.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83a7dab631c78030">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pmcoder" data-paper-title="Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pmcoder-088b3672" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-69e13b18b74254a0">What reusable experience does PMCoder retain across locating, fixing, and testing an issue?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apmcoder">Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Vanderbilt University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A long fix yields clues, failed attempts, and test conclusions. Restarting from the issue repeats searches and mistakes. Phase-organized plans and reads give each step the right history. Memory supports execution but current code and tests still decide if the new issue is fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Remember the parser location and failing boundary input rather than search the whole repo again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06811">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06811-pmcoder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69e13b18b74254a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pmcoder" data-paper-title="Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5a49a3fee65a642">Why condition episodic retrieval on the current phase instead of querying the original issue every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apmcoder">Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Vanderbilt University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Localization, editing, and verification need different evidence. Static retrieval can repeat topically related but phase-inappropriate traces. Hierarchical planning constrains retrieval by phase, detects stalls from behavior, and replans. Real execution verdicts decide whether repair succeeded, not phase changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Localization needs files and verification needs regression tests. Repeatedly searching issue text can keep returning localization experiences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06811">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06811-pmcoder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5a49a3fee65a642">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pmcoder" data-paper-title="Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8b4cfdcf0674ba0">What is the trade-off between trace-based stall detection and rewriting the whole plan after any failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apmcoder">Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Vanderbilt University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trace statistics recognize repeated nonprogress and allow targeted replanning. One failure can be useful evidence rather than a bad direction. Full rewrites repeat work, while never changing can stall indefinitely. Use actual verdicts rather than self-reported recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The same test error after two identical patches suggests another approach. A new first-time error can be normal progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06811">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06811-pmcoder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8b4cfdcf0674ba0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pmcoder" data-paper-title="Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d42348ca21f71f7">Can perfect local phase/retrieval scores be compared with solving 25 more SWE-bench issues?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apmcoder">Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Vanderbilt University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic PlanBench tests phase-conditioned retrieval, stalls, and replanning without repository containers or paper models. Proxy cost is not tool tokens. Report traces and branch evidence rather than call saturation issue-resolution capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Selecting a phase template and completing a three-step fixture does not establish locating, editing, and testing an unknown repository.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06811">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06811-pmcoder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d42348ca21f71f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-codegrep-29277303" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-237d4d1814ad8cbe">Why does CodeGrep treat evidence gathering in large repositories as a learned multi-step task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Before repair, relevant files, symbols, and dependencies may be unknown. One search can retrieve only similar wording. CodeGrep searches, reads, and updates queries from new clues, serving downstream repair. Actual execution determines whether the evidence helped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: grep finds a config entry, but reading it reveals the default is elsewhere. Follow that dependency instead of guessing a local patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-237d4d1814ad8cbe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be1af93d2bb20565">Why reward code retrieval by downstream repair value rather than correct-file hits alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The right file may lack call chains or constraints, and retrieval may be too expensive. Pass evidence to a frozen coding agent and measure actual repair with costs. Freezing the executor reduces co-changing confounds, though one failed repair does not prove a given clue useless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding an erroring function without its caller constraints can still lead to a bad patch. Related files and test context may enable real repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be1af93d2bb20565">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed35b36b766cbf45">How does multi-turn grep, glob, and read differ from one vector Top-K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>grep and glob narrow symbols and paths; reading results informs later queries. This interactive evidence collection differs from fixing candidates by initial embedding similarity. Adaptation costs calls and context, so compare exploration resources as well as file hits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Glob test directories, grep the error symbol, read a caller, then search dependencies based on actual code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed35b36b766cbf45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-28aaa8a73f03f573">What evidence separates local retrieval operators from actual 14B GRPO training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local public mini-suites check bounded selection and state without training a 14B retriever, running SWE-bench, or using the full downstream fixer. Token and turn penalties need real measurements. Registration or simulated search is not executed RL or end-to-end speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two fewer fixture reads are a proxy reduction, not a 1.2-point improvement in actual repairs without real files and generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28aaa8a73f03f573">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-manta-a024f561" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c9e155972b09a66">How can poor communication waste opportunities in a multi-agent team?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More roles do not help if results reach the wrong people, dependencies miss key messages, or ordering is wrong. MANTA adapts communication from execution rather than fixing a roster. Topology changes still cost coordination; evaluate visibility, results, and resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A verifier spots a constraint error but tells an unrelated role. The executor continues on a stale plan; adjust information flow rather than add another agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c9e155972b09a66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12a63e7249c622c4">Why adjust topology edges, ordering, and visibility rather than merely add agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failure can come from missing information, duplicate roles, or absent verification. More agents do not fix these. Trajectories guide bounded changes to relationships and information flow. Budget projection limits communication and execution, and only task feedback confirms gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If reviewers never see current code, fix message visibility rather than add three reviewers of the same stale material.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12a63e7249c622c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ca487177d340d40">What is the trade-off between online topology adaptation and picking a team once at the start?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An initial team uses task priors. Online changes respond to observed bottlenecks, failures, and duplication but can add instability and cost. Project changes onto budgets and permission boundaries rather than add unlimited agents or expose private histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merge duplicate source-checking roles or alter edges, but never let evaluator references reach executors as part of the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ca487177d340d40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fda2c22ac9a171c">What does Π_budget do in topology updates, and what does local evidence establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Project proposed roles, edges, and order changes into allowed resources before execution rather than running an oversized team and accounting for only part of it. The deterministic suite checks state and scheduling without real multi-agent models or environments. Topology change counts are not five-benchmark generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a proposal asks for ten roles but only four fit, construct an executable bounded graph before running, not after omitting six costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fda2c22ac9a171c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cam-df" data-paper-title="CAM-DF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cam-df-2b7f3d23" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-20b5ca35f6a5f4ae">Why decide how many tools to expose after ranking them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acam-df">CAM-DF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rank order does not identify a sufficient set. Too many tools add cost and distraction, while too few miss interfaces. CAM-DF compares virtual prefixes and heterogeneous costs before execution. It controls exposure, not dynamic stopping after actual calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If the first two tools only query and the third modifies, a modification task may need the third regardless of the earlier scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27083-cam-df/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20b5ca35f6a5f4ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cam-df" data-paper-title="CAM-DF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0570cdc0a7c4faa1">Why derive stop labels from the payoff gap between the current prefix and best later prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acam-df">CAM-DF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevance ranking does not say how many exposed tools are sufficient. Early stop can miss capability and late stop costs resources. Virtual payoff subtracts cost from sufficiency; the difference sets stop or continue and its magnitude gives regret. This happens before execution, so virtual payoff is not tool success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two tools already suffice, while a related but expensive third reduces payoff. Stop labels should reflect that cost rather than rank alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27083-cam-df/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0570cdc0a7c4faa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cam-df" data-paper-title="CAM-DF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-580c3367b255c392">How is regret weighting different from ordinary stop/continue labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acam-df">CAM-DF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Error costs can differ. Gap sign supplies the class and magnitude represents lost payoff. Equal weights treat near ties like missed essential tools. A best later prefix is a comparison estimate that depends on sufficiency scoring, not hidden deployment truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Exposing one cheap extra tool has little cost. Stopping before an essential refund interface is a large error that deserves greater weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27083-cam-df/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-580c3367b255c392">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cam-df" data-paper-title="CAM-DF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c90b30ce9f21e6a3">Can local required-tools sufficiency be a general deployment scorer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acam-df">CAM-DF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Required-tools lists in the auditable mini-suite diagnose prefix choices rather than act as a learned semantic scorer. Do not reveal hidden requirements to an evaluated policy. Lower exposure is not live τ-bench token or success improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Knowing the third tool is required is useful for offline payoff, but a runtime router reading that list bypasses the learned sufficiency problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27083-cam-df/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c90b30ce9f21e6a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autoformbot-6fe44000" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edd356cace2c3e7c">Why isn&#x27;t formalizing a whole textbook independent translation of each statement into Lean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later theorems use earlier definitions and lemmas, and work must preserve shared repository state, compilation, and source meaning. AutoFormBot coordinates workers through these dependencies and merges local results into global goals. Compilation only establishes acceptance by the formal system, not faithfulness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A changed foundation can break other proofs even if their branches compiled earlier. Recheck after merging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edd356cace2c3e7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f57c0f41ebcd567f">Why do formalization workers need separate worktrees and a merge queue before checking the global goal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Isolation reduces concurrent file conflicts, the dependency DAG identifies available declarations, and merge review preserves shared consistency. Local Lean success does not cover the entire textbook. The supervisor checks overall progress and replans. Failed experience can become skills, but a branch is not a merged proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two workers prove separate lemmas. Check name collisions and main theorem dependencies after integration before claiming full formalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f57c0f41ebcd567f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e097cb6f2ea1e55">Why isn&#x27;t mechanical compilation a substitute for independent fidelity review?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The Lean kernel checks proofs of formal statements. Added axioms, sorry, weakened claims, or hidden dependencies can bypass the intended problem. Compilation is necessary but not sufficient; verify the original statement, dependencies, and independent review. Completed scheduling is not mathematical fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replacing all natural numbers with zero can make a theorem easy to prove while failing to formalize the original.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e097cb6f2ea1e55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3bee4ada3ee0e2fa">Did the local run execute textbook-scale Lean agents or only record the protocol?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It records the paper&#x27;s methods, dependencies, and costs without Lean jobs, paid calls, training, or GPU runs. A DAG state machine cannot reproduce days and huge token budgets per book. Over forty thousand declarations are author results, and not every book finished.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Scheduling forty goals does not mean forty Lean proofs compiled and passed fidelity review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c5e1155db8327b8">Why does PROMPTS treat model-parallel partitioning as iterative measured optimization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprompts">PROMPTS: Performance Optimization via Multi-Agent Planning for LLM Training and Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training bottlenecks vary by hardware and configuration among compute, memory, and communication. Agents use profiler evidence to propose partitioning and observe effects rather than apply stock settings. A recommendation is not a speedup until measured for runtime, resources, and feasibility on target hardware.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: More sharding may save memory but slow cross-device communication. Profiling distinguishes the bottleneck.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-a638de4eb75357c6">Why ground sharding proposals in profiling rather than retrieving a common best configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprompts">PROMPTS: Performance Optimization via Multi-Agent Planning for LLM Training and Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Optimal parallelism depends on measured compute, communication, and memory constraints. The knowledge base offers options; Analyzer locates bottlenecks, Proposal generates explainable candidates, and Coordinator organizes verification. A config or formula check does not run training or measure speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A configuration is fast on a model card, but local profiling shows all-reduce dominates. Compare options that address communication.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-5bb83b305c81a947">How does separating Coordinator, Analyzer, and Proposal differ from configuration-table search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprompts">PROMPTS: Performance Optimization via Multi-Agent Planning for LLM Training and Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate roles coordinate work, explain bottlenecks, and propose targeted settings from evidence. Table search mainly enumerates predefined options. Multiple agents have their own cost; real training or serving results determine benefit, not explanation length or votes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Analyzer identifies communication as dominant, then Proposal changes sharding accordingly instead of testing every dimension randomly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-a73f467c2768d482">Do local profiler ranking and bounded proposals include TPU/GSPMD measurements?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprompts">PROMPTS: Performance Optimization via Multi-Agent Planning for LLM Training and Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local reference tests cover evidence ranking and proposal constraints without Google TPU profiling, GSPMD, or a production workload matrix. Top-three hits and peak gains are author measurements, not consequences of local candidate ordering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Synthetic profiling can recommend less communication. Until compiling and running that configuration, there is no observed training speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">

<span id="paper-agent-research-paperorchestra-986964dd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-99583ab8b60fcb1e">Why does PaperOrchestra organize actual experiment material into an argument instead of just writing fluent prose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scientific writing connects question, method, evidence, and citations. Fluent text can conceal missing tests or unsupported conclusions. PaperOrchestra coordinates roles to write, verify, and revise from ideas and logs. Automation cannot supply absent validation, and a citation may not support the claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With logs for two datasets, explain those two. Stronger wording cannot create a third experiment or generalization result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99583ab8b60fcb1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dc7aca4108c4bbc">Why can&#x27;t citation checks and revision acceptance replace real experiments and research arguments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citation identity, abstracts, and cutoff checks verify sources and time eligibility. Revision scores constrain edits to existing content. Five writing roles organize actual ideas and logs; they do not create results. Mechanical BibTeX checks and judges are not full literature synthesis or research capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A chart agent can plot real logs, but cannot invent metrics to complete a manuscript. Authentic citations do not make fabricated results true.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dc7aca4108c4bbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-299e40fd9b62b309">Why aren&#x27;t automated judging and human preferences equivalent evidence of writing quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated judges can favor form and fluency, while people assess literature reviews differently. The paper reports weak correlation. Higher revision score still needs factual and dimension-specific checks. One judge improvement does not verify real paper quality or scientific correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: More topical vocabulary may boost automatic scores while misaligned citations and overstated results make experts rate a review worse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-299e40fd9b62b309">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac6886826864233b">What conditions govern citation verification and revision rollback, and what was completed locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citations must match real entities, include abstracts, predate the cutoff strictly, and deduplicate by paper ID. Revert revisions when scores fall or ties regress across subdimensions, at most three rounds. Local work reviews literature and costs without five agents, writing models, or metrics. A BibTeX checker is not literature synthesis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deduplicate two URLs for one paper and exclude post-cutoff research. Valid formatting does not mean the citation supports a sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac6886826864233b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
