<span id="paper-agent-research-aira2-3f4a88e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4269c39e84e5ecd2">Why is automated ML research also an experiment scheduling problem in AIR-A2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents can propose many candidates, but experiments vary in runtime and devices and evaluation are finite. Proposal quality and execution throughput both affect progress. AIR-A2 keeps experiments flowing and manages feedback. Busy workers do not establish research gains; verify selected proposals on isolated evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Waiting for a two-hour experiment can leave devices idle after a ten-minute one finishes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4269c39e84e5ecd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b1a28c04e252ad2">Why does a steady-state worker pool use compute better than waiting for every experiment in a generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experiment lengths differ, so a barrier makes quick workers wait for the slowest. A steady pool assigns the next candidate immediately. Throughput must not alter evaluation isolation: search uses fixed search scores, then untouched validation picks a winner afterward. Do not peek mid-search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three experiments finish in ten minutes and one takes an hour. Reuse idle slots while keeping the predefined data splits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b1a28c04e252ad2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-58f57008467d2ded">Why separate the search split and final validation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search repeatedly uses scores and can overfit by hill climbing. Untouched validation chooses a winner only after search, reducing selection overfitting. Neither is training data, and repeatedly tuning search on validation undermines it. Hidden test stays out of the interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Explore 100 candidates by search ranking, then use the held-out validation once to choose the final model rather than inspect it after every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58f57008467d2ded">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3a6743a353f8dfc">Can 80/10/10 be randomly resplit for every candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One split must be shared so data difficulty does not confound score comparisons. Local tests verify asynchronous scheduling and signal isolation, not multi-H200, Apptainer, or long-running research agents. Rank-based selection probabilities are search rules, not actual performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Identical models can rank differently if one gets easier search samples. A fixed split controls that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3a6743a353f8dfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dynamic-brt-f3fe2d3c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21b0ad9ec1ec3a10">Why is an executable bug-reproduction test valuable before automated repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text issues can be ambiguous. A test makes failure observable and checks whether a patch changes the intended behavior. Dynamic BRT generates and selects tests during repair search. They are local evidence and may lack coverage or overfit a bad patch; they cannot replace full correctness checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reproduce an empty-list crash with a fixed input. After that test passes, independently check other inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21b0ad9ec1ec3a10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc8c2cd9cd8b383e">Why doesn&#x27;t failing on the original bug and passing on a generated patch prove the patch correct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A self-generated test can cover only a local behavior the patch happens to satisfy. Agreement does not establish full semantics. This defines a candidate BRT; stronger evidence needs isolated reference repairs and other verification. Grouping votes by non-test patch keeps different tests from splitting the same fix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A patch returns a constant and its test checks only one matching input. Both conditions pass, but other inputs remain wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc8c2cd9cd8b383e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b670f7557ce5a306">Why group candidates by non-test patch instead of counting each generated test separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fix can pair with several tests. Pairwise votes can split or inflate support for the same code. Group by non-test changes, then choose a test within the majority fix group. Identifier normalization is a heuristic, not a proof of semantic equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten traces with the same code and different assertions are one repair group, not ten independent fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b670f7557ce5a306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d498db4f0ce1da26">Can any execution exception count as a successful bug reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A nonempty assertion must raise assertion_failed on the original, then pass on the fix with acceptable regression results. Syntax errors and unrelated exceptions do not qualify. Execution uses a bounded AST allowlist and timed isolated process, not an arbitrary hostile-code sandbox. Real LLM reviewers and private Google bugs are not run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An import error does not reproduce a business-logic bug just because the patched run imports normally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d498db4f0ce1da26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:watch-and-learn" data-paper-title="Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-watch-and-learn-e9cf239b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-78e1133fbfd419f4">Why use online tutorial videos rather than rely only on expensive action annotations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awatch-and-learn">Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tutorials contain genuine software behavior without machine-readable click coordinates, keys, and actions. Converting visible demonstrations broadens training sources. Frames are not action ground truth: occlusion, edits, and missing typed text can harm conversion and execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file moves across windows, but training data needs to distinguish dragging from a copy command rather than invent a click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04673v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2510.04673-watch-and-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78e1133fbfd419f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:watch-and-learn" data-paper-title="Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d5dc634ef7c4b6c">Why learn inverse dynamics from tutorials instead of treating before/after pixel differences as mouse actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awatch-and-learn">Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Screen changes may come from scrolling, keystrokes, or program responses, so pixels do not identify actions uniquely. The inverse model predicts action type, coordinates, and text from screen pairs, then assembles trajectories. These are estimated labels, not rule guesses or proof an IDM was trained locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A screen can move down from a wheel or a key. Use visual context and supervision instead of labeling every downward shift as a click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04673v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2510.04673-watch-and-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d5dc634ef7c4b6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:watch-and-learn" data-paper-title="Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26c0fe3cc14e615b">What changes when retrieving video examples versus training on annotated trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awatch-and-learn">Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval puts a relevant demonstration in context without updating the executor. SFT writes trajectory patterns into weights. Both rely on IDM label quality, so video count is not correct action count. Similar titles do not establish actual desktop learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use one tutorial as a prompt example or offline training input. Inference cost and how errors propagate differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04673v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2510.04673-watch-and-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26c0fe3cc14e615b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:watch-and-learn" data-paper-title="Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-30274243761e3d5f">Why can&#x27;t one simple rule head replace action, coordinate, and text prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awatch-and-learn">Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper uses action classification, coordinates discretized into 0–1000 classes, and a GPT-2 small autoregressive text head with SigLIP-2 and a four-layer Transformer. Do not invent loss weights. Local work is literature and cost review, not IDM training, corpus download, or desktop evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cursor-difference click rule cannot recover typed text from two frames or replace joint IDM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04673v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2510.04673-watch-and-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30274243761e3d5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolgrad-568745ef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8c8872eb7a3514e">Why does ToolGrad target the cost of high-quality tool trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-step calls need correct interfaces, arguments, and linked results. Human demos cost time and direct model generation can accumulate errors. ToolGrad uses target feedback during dataset construction to repair executable traces. Construction targets must not leak to evaluated agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: During data creation, verify queries reach a known result and fix parameters. At test, gather evidence without reading the answer first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8c8872eb7a3514e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48defda29bfde8a3">Why use answer-conditioned trajectory construction only in data generation, not as evaluated agent input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Known answers support backward construction of tool chains and textual-gradient repair to reduce training annotation. Revealing the target value in evaluation leaks the solution and prevents measuring independent evidence gathering. Training construction information must remain separate from deployed inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use known population to construct API traces for training. At test, give the population question without the reference number.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48defda29bfde8a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-637567167fcf5e81">How does textual gradient differ from a numerical gradient when repairing failed calls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Textual feedback identifies bad arguments, tools, or order and suggests edits; it is not differentiable backpropagation through discrete calls. It depends on feedback quality and execution verification. The name does not imply end-to-end parameter updates, and an edit is not a rerun.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Changing a date format from feedback is text editing. Reinvoke the tool and check its response to verify repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-637567167fcf5e81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b381ff66f4e2605b">Do local answer-first and deduplicated edits cover ToolGrad-12B and BFCL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local references execute backward route construction and deduplicated text repair, without training 12B or running BFCL. Answers stay training-only, execution outcomes must be real, and failures are not backfilled. State transitions do not establish generated-data quality or downstream skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deduplicating two corrections of the same bad argument verifies the edit rule, not automatic correct traces for unknown APIs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b381ff66f4e2605b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolrl" data-paper-title="ToolRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolrl-7e3d5cc8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7dbdad52ce7f9b4a">Why doesn&#x27;t checking only ToolRL&#x27;s final answer establish a good tool policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolrl">ToolRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The result conflates choosing tools, generating arguments, executing, and using outputs. Granular feedback constrains each behavior. Calibrate rewards without letting format or execution hide wrong answers. Local reward computation is not large-model RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A weather tool can be correct but use the wrong city. A single answer score cannot identify argument versus selection failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.13958-toolrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7dbdad52ce7f9b4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolrl" data-paper-title="ToolRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-39b3cc929256b458">Why dynamically scale rewards by tool when their reward difficulties differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolrl">ToolRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High raw rewards from easy tools can dominate updates, burying improvements on harder tools. Center and scale by tool distribution to compare relative performance while retaining selection, argument, execution, and answer signals. Normalization does not fix wrong rewards or equalize actual difficulty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Calculator successes are common and database queries often fail. Normalize separately so easy calculator rewards do not monopolize learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.13958-toolrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39b3cc929256b458">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolrl" data-paper-title="ToolRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-119474e77ea679ab">Why are tool-selection, execution, and answer rewards not substitutes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolrl">ToolRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection checks task fit, execution checks whether a call runs, and answer reward checks final goal. Correct tools can fail from bad arguments, and successful calls can return irrelevant data. Separate signals expose different errors; any one high score does not establish end-to-end ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A database query runs with the wrong month. Selection and execution pass without deserving answer reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.13958-toolrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-119474e77ea679ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolrl" data-paper-title="ToolRL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecda3bd045c50ef5">Do local reward and state updates prove full multi-tool RL training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolrl">ToolRL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local tests cover paper objectives, transitions, and budgets without the original large model, multi-GPU RL, or full real-tool benchmark. Correct reward arithmetic still needs policy sampling, real external execution, and parameter updates. Registration and perfect mini-suites cannot fill those gaps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Computing advantage from four reward dimensions tests an objective, not learned argument generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.13958-toolrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecda3bd045c50ef5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retool" data-paper-title="ReTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-retool-db452677" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-da7a79464de2183e">Why does ReTool learn calling, correction, and stopping together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretool">ReTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tools can help but fail and cost resources. A policy must decide when to call, how to respond to errors, and when evidence suffices. Tool syntax alone does not control a full trajectory. Early stopping and repeated unnecessary calls can both hurt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Run code to check a calculation, fix arguments after an error, then stop once results agree rather than loop or submit unchecked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11536">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.11536-retool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da7a79464de2183e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retool" data-paper-title="ReTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f341f5ec4e371354">Why not learn to avoid tools entirely when calls carry penalties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretool">ReTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The objective also rewards correct answers. Fewer calls matter only if quality does not suffer. Alternating reasoning and actual feedback teaches when to outsource, recover, and stop. Optimizing call count alone may replace needed computation with fluent guesses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Mental arithmetic can avoid calls, but complex statistics need code. One reliable result can be worth more than saving a call and answering incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11536">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.11536-retool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f341f5ec4e371354">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retool" data-paper-title="ReTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-68920b8b5af8933d">How does outcome reward minus call cost compare with one fixed call per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretool">ReTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed counts ignore difficulty and evidence, wasting calls on simple tasks and starving complex ones. Costed rewards adapt counts to value but can suppress needed tools if penalties are excessive. Report correctness and total call costs, not reductions alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Mental arithmetic can use zero calls, while multi-stage calculation may need two checks. One call does not fit both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11536">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.11536-retool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68920b8b5af8933d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retool" data-paper-title="ReTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-888b668a9e5c1718">Can the model fill in a tool observation to complete a reasoning/action trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretool">ReTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Actual tool or environment execution must supply feedback. The model generates its reasoning and actions only. Fabricated outputs remove learning evidence for calls and corrections. Local controlled state/budget tests do not train the paper model or run real math benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Writing &#x27;Python output: 42&#x27; without running code is neither tool success nor grounds for execution reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11536">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.11536-retool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-888b668a9e5c1718">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openhands" data-paper-title="OpenHands" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-openhands-e21fcd2c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-718d5bd7d13021cc">Why is OpenHands a software-agent work platform for editing, execution, and browsing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenhands">OpenHands</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · All-Hands-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real software tasks require inspecting files, commands, pages, and continuing long workflows, not only generating code. OpenHands connects operations to feedback in a consistent environment. Platform support and a controller&#x27;s ability are separate evidence; tools alone do not make policies reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After editing a frontend, start the service, inspect the page, and return to code when it fails. Code generation alone misses that loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2407.16741-openhands/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-718d5bd7d13021cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openhands" data-paper-title="OpenHands" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7201d318abb3e27c">Why does a unified event stream make editor, terminal, and browser workflows auditable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenhands">OpenHands</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · All-Hands-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions and sandbox returns enter one timeline. Policies continue from observed results and reviewers can trace changes and validation. Shared events do not erase tool-specific semantics or establish code safety and correctness. Isolation, permissions, and tests have distinct roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Editor events change a file, terminal events run tests, and browser events check a page. The stream shows whether tests preceded or followed edits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2407.16741-openhands/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7201d318abb3e27c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openhands" data-paper-title="OpenHands" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9579dd55c1112b36">Why are platform runtime and agent controller distinct contributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenhands">OpenHands</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · All-Hands-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The runtime supplies actions, observations, and isolation. A controller chooses plans and tool usage; different policies can share one platform. Running editor and terminal verifies execution paths, not full model reasoning or official SWE-bench resolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A script and LLM may use the same sandbox without equal issue understanding or repair ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2407.16741-openhands/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9579dd55c1112b36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openhands" data-paper-title="OpenHands" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-56484f867d35a859">Does a local browser interface mean real web interaction is connected?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenhands">OpenHands</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · All-Hands-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work emits editor events and runs fixed regressions in an isolated temp directory. Browser action semantics are retained without a live environment or full controller. Claim only observed events and outcomes, not real navigation from a type definition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Recording browser_open does not open a page, fetch its DOM, or click an element. Those require real browser evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2407.16741-openhands/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56484f867d35a859">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-agent" data-paper-title="SWE-agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-swe-agent-79904a33" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-260212a2f996528e">Why does a GitHub issue agent need a convenient repository viewing and editing interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-agent">SWE-agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model must locate unknown code, read needed context, make small edits, and verify. Raw terminal output can be long or fragile. SWE-agent&#x27;s interface better fits that workflow without replacing issue understanding or tests. A successful command does not mean resolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Open matching files and relevant lines rather than printing the repository, then run the target tests after edits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-260212a2f996528e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-agent" data-paper-title="SWE-agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dafefde79785114c">Why can a specialized ACI work better than an unrestricted shell?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-agent">SWE-agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broad actions and verbose output increase selection and localization load. An ACI makes search, viewing, precise edits, and tests easier to act on and interpret. This improves the repository interaction contract, not hidden patch access. Real tests still verify completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Showing nearby lines and an exact replacement makes editing easier than printing a whole file, but regression tests must validate the patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dafefde79785114c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-agent" data-paper-title="SWE-agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-99e902304d6ed5e3">Why compare ACI with raw shell using the same model and tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-agent">SWE-agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise stronger models or easier tasks confound interface effects. ACI changes action and observation boundaries, so control other conditions and assess actual patches and tests. One good edit or valid command syntax cannot establish broad repair ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Give the same model the same bug with a narrow editor versus a raw shell to isolate differences in localization and editing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99e902304d6ed5e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:swe-agent" data-paper-title="SWE-agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52983128b5e50c57">What do the initial failure and fixed unittest prove in local swebench-local?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aswe-agent">SWE-agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A real initial failure shows a problem exists. The exit code after editing verifies the covered regression. Local tools only read files, write solution.py, and run fixed tests. This is executable micro-benchmark evidence, not official SWE-bench Lite or broader coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Fixing arithmetic until one suite passes verifies the edit-and-run path, not official GitHub issue resolved rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autogen-60994f2d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-520344c861492850">Why does AutoGen organize multi-agent applications as programmable conversations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Models, execution tools, and people may need repeated feedback beyond one question and answer. Configurable roles and messages let tool results or replies trigger later steps. Role names are not collaboration ability; specify responders, handoff, stop conditions, and actual artifact checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An assistant proposes code, an executor returns an error, and the assistant revises under a protocol rather than endless chat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-520344c861492850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47f466dc66f53411">Why does conversation programming need explicit termination instead of endless role replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Messages can keep triggering responses. Without responsibilities, tool boundaries, and stopping rules, collaboration can repeat or loop. Conversation programming composes these controls for group and nested chats. More roles do not guarantee effective division; completion still needs verified artifacts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A writer and reviewer repeatedly suggest improvements. Define a stop after verification passes or budget ends.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47f466dc66f53411">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8669aba9d7a12d1d">How does message-driven orchestration differ from a fixed linear script?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A linear script predefines one order. Message policies choose recipients, nested conversations, and stopping based on state or content. Flexibility helps tools and humans collaborate but can add useless chatter and loops. More messages or roles do not prove gains; count their costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A failed review can trigger one nested repair, while a pass ends immediately instead of always running five turns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8669aba9d7a12d1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d058576a8a28231">Does the local planner/executor/critic protocol run the full AutoGen runtime?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements deterministic handoff, message logs, and stopping without full runtime, real LLM group chat, or container execution. Round counts verify the protocol; perfect scores are not the paper&#x27;s multi-application ability or development efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One rule-based message per role can pass a protocol without solving an open software task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d058576a8a28231">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-metagpt-ffaa73e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-843bb845fe7721da">Why does MetaGPT organize agents around software roles and deliverables?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requirements, design, implementation, and testing depend on each other. Free chat can distort handoffs. MetaGPT gives roles explicit responsibilities and checkable artifacts. Organization helps but complete documents are not correct code; run verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An architect defines the interface, engineers implement it, and testers check it. Chat-only definitions can lead to inconsistent parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-843bb845fe7721da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03055a1e793d577f">Why can structured artifacts reduce hallucination cascades compared with free role chat?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Downstream roles consume requirements, designs, and test contracts whose fields and constraints can be checked instead of trusting verbal promises. SOPs define order and dependencies so faults are easier to locate. Valid format does not ensure correct content or usable software; verify and execute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An architect&#x27;s interface lets engineers check signatures. &#x27;The design is done&#x27; lets every role imagine a different contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03055a1e793d577f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f75b36d8fc81d025">How is PM, Architect, Engineer, and QA specialization different from repeated self-paraphrase?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each stage has distinct inputs, outputs, and artifacts: requirements, design, implementation, and tests. Gains depend on contracts and feedback, not labels that merely sound independent. Shared wrong assumptions can still break every stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: QA should run tests rather than rephrase the engineer&#x27;s claim that the code looks correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f75b36d8fc81d025">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad3ab6d711ba69e5">How does the local temporary-repository test differ from a full MetaGPT LLM team?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Four roles leave structured artifacts; engineering actually edits Python and QA runs fixed unittest. Full LLM collaboration and official SWE-bench are absent. This supports an auditable execution path, not HumanEval, MBPP, or real team delivery rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file hash and test output verify one change and run, not autonomous architecture for unknown requirements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad3ab6d711ba69e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolbench" data-paper-title="ToolBench" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolbench-89c52f4b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a0f6c07e30bff56">Why teach a model multiple tools rather than handwrite calls for each ToolBench task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolbench">ToolBench</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real catalogs have varied interfaces and parameters. A model must understand intent, find relevant demonstrations, and generate executable calls. ToolBench studies data and constraints for transferable tool use. Format is one step; verify API behavior, outputs, and final answers rather than synthetic success alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Weather and map tools require different fields. Use each contract instead of copying one fixed template.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16504">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16504-toolbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a0f6c07e30bff56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolbench" data-paper-title="ToolBench" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-effa1825464a63ea">Why constrain format and check real execution in addition to retrieving usage examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolbench">ToolBench</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Examples show when and how to call tools but cannot guarantee schema or argument meaning. Format constraints ensure parseability; execution tests whether the goal is achieved. Experience, contracts, and observed results are distinct. JSON-like text is not actual tool capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A complete weather-call schema can still name the wrong city. Valid JSON does not answer the requested forecast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16504">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16504-toolbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-effa1825464a63ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolbench" data-paper-title="ToolBench" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f0d05b126401e20">How does retrieving in-context demonstrations differ from always using one fixed example set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolbench">ToolBench</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval chooses examples for the current task, avoiding irrelevant context and broader coverage gaps of fixed examples. It can still choose badly or encourage copied arguments. Reuse procedures, not answers. Compare fixed models and tasks and include example-reading cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: SQL examples help database queries more than weather samples, but their table names cannot be reused unverified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16504">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16504-toolbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f0d05b126401e20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolbench" data-paper-title="ToolBench" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b063717d0acaa6b">Does local planbench-mini tool success equal the paper&#x27;s eight tasks or live API success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolbench">ToolBench</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work tests demonstration, constraint, or state protocols without paper-scale models, training, or the full real tool matrix. Tool results and scoring require independent execution. Perfect controlled results are not public benchmark scores, and similarly named ToolBench datasets must not be conflated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A preset plan can parse and execute without proving the model can call an unseen service from documentation.</p>
