<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16504">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16504-toolbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b063717d0acaa6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:critic" data-paper-title="CRITIC" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-critic-11dab3d3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bafd7c35b893a5b8">Why does CRITIC try to find and fix errors after the model has already written an answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acritic">CRITIC</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Drafts can contain factual, reasoning, or code errors despite confidence. CRITIC gathers external checks for critique and revision. Observable evidence helps, but tools have limited coverage and edits can add errors. Evaluate checks and final outcomes separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Execute code on a boundary input, observe an exception, and revise. Rereading the same explanation gives no equivalent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.11738-critic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bafd7c35b893a5b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:critic" data-paper-title="CRITIC" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1766e55c41f638fd">Why can external tool feedback reveal persistent errors that rereading an answer misses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acritic">CRITIC</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-critique may inherit the original model&#x27;s assumptions. Search facts or code outputs provide independently observable constraints. Evidence guides revision in a loop. Tools can fail or return nothing; no feedback is not verification, and success must not be fabricated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A wrong product may still look right to the model. A calculator result provides a concrete contradiction for revision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.11738-critic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1766e55c41f638fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:critic" data-paper-title="CRITIC" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d28a5a81f959747">What evidence does code execution provide for critique versus web retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acritic">CRITIC</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Execution shows outputs or exceptions for a specific input. Web retrieval supplies external text whose source and support must be assessed. Both extend self-evaluation, with different limits: untested code can still fail, and a search hit need not support the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Division by zero proves one run failed. A related web result still needs its actual passage read, not just its title.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.11738-critic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d28a5a81f959747">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:critic" data-paper-title="CRITIC" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-72d92522b177ffce">What feedback does the local real-traceback loop cover?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acritic">CRITIC</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It writes a defective patch, runs unittest, edits from observed feedback, reruns, and records commands and exit codes each round. This verifies controlled code feedback and iteration, not search engines, toxicity classifiers, or a general LLM critic. Running tests does not validate all paper tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A second patch turning a failed test into a pass verifies this code instance, not open-domain QA or harmlessness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.11738-critic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72d92522b177ffce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:camel" data-paper-title="CAMEL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-camel-640cbec7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-707d4c87b3c8e6c6">Why does CAMEL study role collaboration instead of only a single model answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acamel">CAMEL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some tasks need requests, actions, and feedback over time. Two constrained roles can produce a longer collaboration process and data. Dialogue length and role division do not prove quality; roles can misunderstand goals, repeat, or drift. Inspect outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One role requests analysis and another implements with feedback. Repeating the request across turns does not complete the analysis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17760-camel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-707d4c87b3c8e6c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:camel" data-paper-title="CAMEL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03d873922f3e2ffc">Why is inception prompting with roles, goals, and boundaries more than naming two models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acamel">CAMEL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompts define responsibilities, permitted requests, and cooperation. Alternating messages advance a common task under constraints. Renaming without capability or boundary differences can produce duplicates rather than collaboration. A social trace does not prove goal achievement; check deliverables separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One role specifies implementation and the other proposes solutions without changing the overall goal. Mutual praise does not move the task forward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17760-camel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03d873922f3e2ffc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:camel" data-paper-title="CAMEL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dda7e7980ef7bf0">What does alternating two-role cooperation trade off against one complete model response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acamel">CAMEL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dialogue can clarify and divide reasoning, but adds turns, communication, and error propagation. Models sharing biases cannot validate one another by agreement. Evaluate task outcomes and total cost rather than natural-sounding social messages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An executor can ask for missing input. If both roles misread the goal, more turns only extend the mistake.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17760-camel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dda7e7980ef7bf0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:camel" data-paper-title="CAMEL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1991aa1d4d0cf319">Does the local collaboration state machine match the full paper&#x27;s multi-agent instruction-following scope?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acamel">CAMEL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · King Abdullah University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests role messages, state updates, and budget without full large-model social traces or benchmarks. Scripted lines can verify handoffs but not autonomous cooperation or general open-task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two templated replies show alternation works, not that models maintain role and goal boundaries on unfamiliar tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17760-camel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1991aa1d4d0cf319">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hugginggpt" data-paper-title="HuggingGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hugginggpt-c07a7bb7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-898d4e2f2bf49825">Why does HuggingGPT use expert model descriptions as a searchable capability catalog?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahugginggpt">HuggingGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The controller matches subtasks to model-card descriptions and invokes experts instead of implementing all vision and speech itself. Descriptions guide selection, not guarantee capability. Verify versions, input/output types, and availability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Object recognition calls detection; audio-to-text calls ASR. Their media and output contracts differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17580-hugginggpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-898d4e2f2bf49825">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hugginggpt" data-paper-title="HuggingGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9a80e3694f3511f">Why obey subtask dependencies instead of calling all multimodal experts simultaneously?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahugginggpt">HuggingGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A later expert may require actual outputs from detection, recognition, or transcription. Build a DAG, select compatible experts, run in topological order, then synthesize. Similar names do not imply compatible interfaces. Parallelize independent work, not dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Translate only after receiving real speech transcription. Starting translation concurrently and guessing the transcript breaks provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17580-hugginggpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9a80e3694f3511f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hugginggpt" data-paper-title="HuggingGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-070cfaf4dcda6378">What does the language controller do versus a specialist multimodal model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahugginggpt">HuggingGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The controller interprets requests, selects specialists, and schedules subtasks. Specialists process vision or audio and the controller synthesizes results. Correct routing does not ensure correct predictions, and individual predictions do not guarantee a correct final answer. Verify selection, I/O, and interpretation separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A controller schedules image recognition before speech generation. The image and speech models execute their roles; the controller does not acquire their parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17580-hugginggpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-070cfaf4dcda6378">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hugginggpt" data-paper-title="HuggingGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-974376ffc686eefe">Do the local capability registry and dependency edges run downloaded expert models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahugginggpt">HuggingGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local tool descriptions replace the model catalog to check matching and topological execution. No hundreds of Hugging Face checkpoints or ChatGPT calls ran. Edge counts verify flow, not cross-modal quality or real costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A detection node&#x27;s rule-generated output can reach the answer node without establishing actual vision recognition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.17580-hugginggpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-974376ffc686eefe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-art-62b00229" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8434f90df5880a2">Why does ART reuse reasoning and tool demonstrations for new tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Handwriting full CoT and tool flows for each task is costly. Prior examples offer transferable structure. ART retrieves examples and generates workflows using external computation. Validate current inputs and actual outputs; copying old answers or assuming cross-domain transfer is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reuse a calculator-based cost comparison procedure for a new bill, but obtain new numbers and execution results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8434f90df5880a2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-16afeb1e858f4dd5">Why pause at a tool marker and resume after execution instead of generating a whole program with results at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pausing conditions later text on real tool returns rather than imagined outcomes. Retrieved reasoning/tool examples reduce manual prompts, but the runner must detect markers and inject observations. Frozen weights do not prevent tool feedback changing context and future output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Execute a database query at its marker, then summarize the three returned rows rather than claim ten and add an unrun query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16afeb1e858f4dd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-64e08257bb08b925">What is the trade-off between retrieving examples automatically and hand-writing CoT for each task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval reuses library patterns and reduces human authoring, but similar examples may miss current constraints. Human revisions can extend the library, and new programs still need verification. Copying an example does not solve a new task or eliminate maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reuse search-then-compute structure, but use queries and arguments from the new problem rather than copy the old answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64e08257bb08b925">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e15636c7c6d5f1c">How does the local tool-signature task bank differ from program generation by a frozen LLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local tests check small-library retrieval, per-tool pause/resume, and updates without a frozen large model or BIG-Bench/MMLU. Pause counts show branches ran, not model-generated program semantics. Proxy costs are not paper tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three pauses from a structured template test the runner, not automatic programming for arbitrary natural language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e15636c7c6d5f1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolformer-dc9c6efa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-941bf8191f60f91a">Why learn when to use external tools from text training in Toolformer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fluent models may still struggle with arithmetic, fresh facts, or retrieval. Toolformer inserts helpful API calls into training so the model learns timing, arguments, and return usage. Screening supplies learning signals, not guaranteed usefulness. A local filter does not train the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Insert a calculator call when a multiplication result helps complete the sentence, not after every number.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-941bf8191f60f91a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf11c35f247b81e0">Why compare later loss with the API return visible, hidden, and without a call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Call syntax alone can look useful without tool information. Counterfactual return conditions test whether actual output lowers later prediction loss. Keep calls beating the threshold for training to learn utility. This self-supervised proxy is not universal task accuracy or business gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Calculator syntax does not reveal the product. If the real return improves subsequent prediction, keep that call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf11c35f247b81e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-50aa9ed63c22b586">How does Toolformer construct call data differently from manually labeled tool trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human examples directly demonstrate actions. Toolformer starts with a few demonstrations, samples calls, filters by how much returns improve subsequent text prediction, then trains on retained data. This reduces per-call annotation without eliminating demonstrations, tools, or filtering requirements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Instead of manually tagging each calculator call, generate candidates and filter by loss. Some bad candidates still need rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50aa9ed63c22b586">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a4db4174ad5d40b">Why isn&#x27;t local utility-loss filtering completed GPT-J continued training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local loss comes from deterministic utility. It preserves the candidate rule without GPT-J token likelihood, 6.7B training, or five real API classes. Candidate and acceptance counts show filtering ran, not learned timing or paper zero-shot capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A preset useful tool lowering rule-based loss verifies screening, not discovery of tool value in real training text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a4db4174ad5d40b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pal-f0f14e4c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e1c7b8a77c3e843">Why does PAL generate programs and leave calculation to an interpreter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Word problems require both interpreting relationships and exact computation. Models turn interpretation into runnable code and the interpreter handles arithmetic. This reduces manual calculation burden, assuming the program captures the task. Execution cannot detect omitted conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Assign people and prices to variables, but forgetting a half-price child means accurate execution of an incorrect total.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e1c7b8a77c3e843">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9d3e89879637bdf">Why can PAL still answer incorrectly after delegating arithmetic to Python?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deterministic runtime executes the given program, not the intended problem. The model still represents variables, relations, and control flow. Wrong units or discount order yield precisely wrong results. PAL reduces arithmetic errors without eliminating modeling mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The task discounts the subtotal before shipping, but code discounts both. Execution is correct for the wrong formula.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9d3e89879637bdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94f7d51c0584d5a3">How do error sources differ in PAL and manual chain-of-thought arithmetic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CoT handles understanding, steps, and arithmetic together. PAL gives exact arithmetic to programs, reducing numerical mistakes but introducing code and interface errors. Inspect intermediates and verify inputs and formulas. Determinism alone cannot predict accuracy or cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An interpreter avoids multiplication mistakes, but treating a tax rate as a monetary amount remains a modeling error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94f7d51c0584d5a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bc0289c64e50fec">Is the local CALL/RETURN intermediate representation arbitrary Python execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A controlled interpreter verifies program construction and execution separation without Codex or paper GSM8K. Narrow actions help check contracts but do not establish open Python synthesis or a general security sandbox.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Predefined CALL nodes do not cover arbitrary loops, files, or external dependencies in a real runtime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bc0289c64e50fec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mrkl-816ab670" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7fbb257a95880c3">Why does MRKL combine an LLM with several external experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open questions can need language understanding, precise calculation, database access, or specialized knowledge. The LLM routes work and integrates results. Modularity separates capability sources but introduces routing and interface risks. One reliable module does not make the whole system reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Fetch a balance from a database, calculate the difference, then explain it. Querying the wrong account invalidates even exact arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7fbb257a95880c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b8ae0b3087063fb">Why doesn&#x27;t routing to deterministic modules guarantee a correct system answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calculators and databases are reliable only within their contracts. Routers may choose the wrong module or inputs, and language synthesis can misread outputs. MRKL separates precise capabilities from generation. Local determinism and end-to-end correctness are different guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A calculator receives an incorrect tax rate. Its result is precise and reproducible but wrong for the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b8ae0b3087063fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ffb366fa4415fbc">What do modular experts trade off against one LLM doing everything?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts can improve control of exact computation or fresh knowledge. One LLM has simpler interfaces but can rely on stale internal guesses. Routing, conversions, and errors add modular costs and depend on expert coverage. A calculator does not confer provable whole-system correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A calendar computes the date difference; explaining why something was delayed still needs language and evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ffb366fa4415fbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-559b994dc46c150a">Do local specialist call counts include Jurassic-X or a real knowledge base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic calculator and calendar specialists test routing and counts without Jurassic-X, search, or private databases. Proxy cost is not online latency. Symbolic call counts do not establish open QA or fresh knowledge quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fixture database record tests scheduling, not real permissions, failures, or data updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-559b994dc46c150a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-saycan-7674e520" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29c0976bcc5a61c">Why can&#x27;t a robot directly execute a plausible language-model plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language reasoning may not know robot position, skill limits, or physical conditions. SayCan connects task meaning to affordance, selecting related and feasible next steps. Feasibility estimates can err, so report simulated plans separately from real completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Getting a cup is semantically right for a drink request, but the robot may need an executable approach step if it cannot reach the cup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29c0976bcc5a61c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff44151b17aba420">Why multiply language relevance by affordance to filter plausible but impossible actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language scoring measures fit to instructions and history; the value function estimates execution success in the current world. Both need to be high. Language alone can suggest unreachable objects, and feasibility alone can pick irrelevant skills. Coverage and value estimates still limit selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cup in a locked cabinet is relevant but not directly graspable. Opening the cabinet first can score better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff44151b17aba420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-878039f33300c8bc">Why are plan success and execution success different robot metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sound plan can fail through perception, grasp, or control errors. Execution includes physical risk. SayCan reports both; higher planning rates are not completion rates. A deterministic local gate does not cover real control failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a cup and placing it on a table is a valid plan. A slipping gripper still makes execution fail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-878039f33300c8bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-449b830f70953589">Do local affordance checks validate real value-function training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic feasibility filters required and distractor skills while preserving two-score step selection. No vision, robot policy, or value network was trained. Check counts show execution paths, not calibrated success predictions or physical task results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule can block grasping with a full hand without estimating reachability from images or grasp probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-449b830f70953589">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-webgpt-13267288" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc127a045c60084f">Why does WebGPT include browsing and source support in long-form QA rather than rely on memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebgpt">WebGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open questions can need current facts and multiple sources. Browsing collects evidence for cited answers, and human feedback rates quality. Retrieved text still needs interpretation. Citation count neither proves support for individual claims nor covers all material facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Comparing two policies requires both primary descriptions. One related link cannot support every figure in the paragraph.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2112.09332-webgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc127a045c60084f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb490f6e472d9e28">Why rank citation-bearing browsing trajectories by human preference instead of simply requiring links?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebgpt">WebGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A URL does not guarantee support or answer quality. Behavior cloning learns browser actions, then preference reward selects better trajectories. Citations are checkable entry points, but selective quoting or unvisited sources are not reliable and must map to claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two answers cite the same article; one reports the date correctly and one overstates its conclusion. Link counts cannot distinguish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2112.09332-webgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb490f6e472d9e28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-849870cabbf2c4b0">What roles do behavior cloning and human-preference rejection sampling play?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebgpt">WebGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cloning learns search, browsing, and answering from demonstrations. A preference model ranks and selects among candidate trajectories. Selection does not create facts, and can incur judge bias and sampling cost. Best-of-64 is not a single-call efficiency comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Choosing one of 64 responses may improve preference scores while paying for multiple browsing and generation runs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2112.09332-webgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-849870cabbf2c4b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f15afaaf211da371">Is choosing between two local trajectories by evidence coverage equivalent to live browsing and a reward model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebgpt">WebGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local checks retain browse actions, citation constraints, and candidate selection without live web, GPT-3 training, or a human preference model. Controlled coverage cannot be renamed human win rate, TruthfulQA, or real web fact verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Selecting a preset trace with broader evidence tests rejection sampling, not the full system without real pages and preference scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2112.09332-webgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f15afaaf211da371">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retrace" data-paper-title="ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-retrace-4241a794" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-38a1fb8c38cf06c9">Does ReTrace&#x27;s planner-free claim forbid every model call in the system?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretrace">ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Columbia University / Amazon internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Code selects the next step without per-step LLM planning, but a fixed tool may internally use a model, such as a document classifier. The local IR only emits typed calls and does not execute even those tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a guard selects an invoice-classification node that uses a model; subsequent dispatch still depends on code and returned state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38a1fb8c38cf06c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retrace" data-paper-title="ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a436de21ccb70a1">Why must a ReTrace guard not read the result of the tool it is about to call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretrace">ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Columbia University / Amazon internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The condition must be decidable before the action, otherwise it leaks future information. Arguments must bind to inputs, already observed results or constants. Missing observations cause explicit failure rather than plausible invented values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: shipping status is known only after querying the order. That unknown result cannot decide whether to issue the query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a436de21ccb70a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retrace" data-paper-title="ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4650369503d2ebd">Why are ReTrace rule compilation and Toolformer API-call filtering different forms of tool learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretrace">ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Columbia University / Amazon internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Toolformer filters useful calls by downstream token loss with returned evidence and continues model training. ReTrace recovers conditions from SOPs and reasoning traces to create code-controlled workflows. One changes model-generated calls; the other relocates step selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: training a model to request exchange rates when useful differs from a cited guard saying to query rates when currencies differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4650369503d2ebd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:retrace" data-paper-title="ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52c873cdc3b398ba">Why preserve an unwitnessed ReTrace branch without calling it validated in a real environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aretrace">ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Columbia University / Amazon internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some alternatives are supported by SOPs or reasoning but absent from executed traces. Keeping the marker avoids silently dropping them; a citation does not establish successful execution. Local coverage checks dispatch, argument types and provenance, not real tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: an SOP says to escalate when offline, but no training run is offline. Preserve the branch without inventing an offline success rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52c873cdc3b398ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

With a plan in hand, how does an agent choose tools, interpret results, and share reliable execution state across roles?

## Takeaway

Tool calls need a contract: when to call, parameters, how outputs affect next actions, and how failures are recorded. Toolformer uses later prediction loss to filter useful API calls. CRITIC uses external feedback to revise answers. Collaboration adds ownership, state handoffs, and artifact verification. Role count is organizational; information flow, responsibility, and actual tool execution determine results.

## Example

For a repository fix, a search role locates code, an execution role edits and tests, and a reviewer reads the real diff and test output. A timed-out command is not success. Separate environment failure from an incorrect fix. Three roles saying it looks right do not replace an executable check.

## Common pitfall

Tool output is evidence to verify and may be stale, injected, or incomplete. Limit permissions, keep failures and unknowns, and avoid repeating actions with side effects. Local interfaces, candidate filtering, and small environments do not establish full browser, production, or software benchmark capability.

## Reading order

Read Toolformer for deciding when a call helps, CRITIC for evidence-driven revision, and SWE-agent for stateful repository actions and test loops.

1. [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)
2. [CRITIC](../../../../agent-research/2305.11738-critic/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738)
3. [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)

## Check your understanding

One role writes a patch, another agrees, and a third declares success. With no test execution record, is verification complete?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Roles can share one error. Define acceptance conditions, run relevant checks, and read the results. Keep unrun and interrupted checks separate. If execution is unavailable, report static review only; role discussion is not a passing test.

</details>
